items: FICA is withheld at 7.65 per cent of gross pay, and the shop owes the same amount again as its own expense.
Amounts withheld from the two employees are liabilities until they are remitted; the shop's own share is Payroll Tax Expense. Keeping those apart is the single most common payroll error.

Shop time booked to a numbered job is direct labour and goes to that job. Shop time spent sweeping, moving stock, sharpening and setting machines is indirect and belongs to factory overhead. The showroom and office wage is neither: it is an expense of the period.

The proprietor is not on the payroll. A sole proprietor is not an employee of their own business, so the owner keeps no time card, the owner's labour never reaches a job, and money the owner takes out is a withdrawal of capital, not a wage.

The payroll covers 1 to 15 December. The shop works on to the eighteenth, and those three days are not paid until the end of the month, so no wages for 16, 17 and 18 December appear in these books, which is as it should be for a trial balance taken before the adjusting entries.

blocks.text: Ashgrove makes what it sells, so cost is built up job by job before any of it becomes an expense. Lumber, panel, hardware and finish are bought into Raw Materials. As a job needs them they are requisitioned out of Raw Materials and into Work in Process; the hours booked to the job and its share of factory overhead go into Work in Process too. When the job is finished it moves, at what it accumulated, into Finished Goods. Only when it is delivered and invoiced does that cost leave Finished Goods for Cost of Goods Sold.

Every kitchen and every stair rail has a number, a production order and a cost sheet. The requisitions and time tickets in the envelope say which job each one belongs to, and the cost sheets together must always equal the Work in Process account. The shop closed for the last week of November and finished everything on the bench first, so Work in Process opens at nil: nothing on 18 December was carried in from last month.

Overhead is actual, not a rate set in advance. The fortnight's factory overhead is charged to the jobs in proportion to the direct labour on each one's cost sheet, so that the Factory Overhead account empties. Factory Wages is a clearing account for the same reason: the week's shop wages go in, and the entry that splits them between the jobs, the shop and the showroom takes them out again.
